prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
**[goal]** Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` hooks run in order, always run, and a failing hook isn't silently ignored.

**[action]** Root cause: `emit` in `src/bus.ts` used `list.forEach(async (handler) => { await handler(payload); })`. `forEach` never awaits the async callback, so (a) async handlers ran concurrently — interleaving broke subscription order, (b) `emit` resolved before handlers finished (plugin's async redaction sometimes lost the race; "a hook never runs" = its promise was never awaited), (c) thrown/rejected errors became unhandled rejections — silently ignored, and (d) iterating the live array made mid-emit unsubscribes splice the list and skip handlers. Fixed `emit` to snapshot the list at start and `await` each handler in a `for...of` loop — sequential, in order, resolves after all, first failure rejects `emit` and stops the rest, mid-emit unsubscribes count from the next emit. Public API unchanged; tests in `test/` and `package.json` untouched (no dependencies added).

**[result]** Evidence:
- `node --test` → `pass 2, fail 0` (both existing tests, unchanged).
- Scratch verification (`Temp\opencode\hook-bus-verify.ts`, outside the workspace) exercising every README clause → `ALL PASS`: (1) sequential order `a-start,a-end,b-start,b-end`, (2) `emit` resolves only after all handlers settle, (3) sync throw rejects `emit` with the same error and later handlers don't run, (4) async rejection propagates, (5) mid-emit unsubscribe still runs the snapshot handler, gone from next emit, (6) self-unsubscribing one-time handler fires once, (7) `registerAuditPlugin` end-to-end: audit log is `["notice: tool output is audited", "shell: run password=[redacted] done"]` — notice first, redacted output second.
- One scratch-script assertion was wrong on my side (`password=\S+` stops at whitespace, so `password=a b` → `password=[redacted] b`); the bus behavior was correct and I fixed the expectation, then re-ran: `ALL PASS`.

**[next]** Assumptions stated: "runs the handlers that were subscribed when it started" I read as a snapshot, i.e. a handler that unsubscribes itself still runs in that emit (the plugin's one-time notice confirms that reading). Nothing open: public API, test files, and `package.json` are byte-identical to before; no browser tabs, windows, or apps were opened, so nothing to close.
